subject: desertOasisDiorama
pitch:
Category: Diorama.
Subject: desert oasis with palms, tents and camels.
Style: low-poly whimsical mix.
reasoning:
Looking at the renders, I'm checking why the lowest point sits 135mm below y=0 when the base lathe and root joint should start near zero -- likely some leg or hoof geometry extending below the intended base.

Still working out the dune clamping math...

Checking the base lathe geometry confirms the dune stays within radius bounds near the bottom. Now I'm shifting to examining the camel identity—the heads look off, with odd spiky mane tufts and cone-shaped ears that make them resemble horses or llamas more than camels, though the hump reads correctly.

The eyes are also oddly placed, sitting too high near a brow ridge, and the close-up of the neck shows large dark spikes jutting sideways that look more like mane armor than fur.

I'm shortening and thinning those spikes, confining them under the throat for a shaggy-camel look rather than along the whole neck, and also reconsidering the head's facing direction since the overall orientation still seems off.

Now I'm double-checking how the head coordinates compose with the scaling and yaw transform, verifying the local offsets for hair features stay consistent with the point-projection function so the proportions hold once everything is scaled.

Looking at the camel's proportions, the neck height relative to the body seems reasonable, but I'm noticing the ears look too large and horn-like given their current length and angle, so I'm considering shrinking them into shorter, flatter shapes for a more natural look. I'm also starting to check the eye placement next.

The palms are tall and dominate the scene, partially occluding the camels which end up tiny. I'm considering reducing palm heights by about 15% and scaling the camels up by 1.25x to make them more of a visual hero in the composition.

Checking the repositioned camel coordinates against the base radius, camel1 at (-0.55,0.55) risks edge clipping once scaled, so I'm pulling positions inward and dialing the scale back slightly to k=1.2 — camel1 to (-0.5,0.48), camel2 to (0,0.68) — while confirming camel2 stays clear of the fire and pond zones.

Checking the remaining palm trunk heights against the bunting connections and tent pole positions, those all stay consistent. I'll adjust the frond size threshold slightly, from h > 0.7 to h > 0.65, which should work fine.

Now looking at the back view, the camels hide behind the palm and tent 1's flat back looks okay, but the teal ridge tent in the three-quarter view looks off—the extruded prism sides appear striped and the rear gable reads as a dull beige-gray mix rather than the intended color. The door texture also isn't visible from the three-quarter angle since it's positioned on the opposite end from what's shown in the front view, though the tent itself otherwise seems acceptable.

Checking the pole and ridge placements, the front poles holding the lantern beyond the awning line up fine, and the fire cauldron with its black pot and pinkish glowing flame cone looks reasonable. The camels' black knee-pad dots look strange though—I want to swap that for a darker coat tone or a lighter hoof color instead, since the current black balls read oddly against the thin stick legs.

Looking closer at the camel proportions, I'm noting the head and neck mane spikes need resizing, so I'm planning several fixes: clamping the dune soundness warning, adjusting camel scale and positions, shrinking the mane spikes and ears, enlarging the eyes, recoloring the knee pads, and lowering the palms. I also want to make the humps bulge more prominently since the current size barely reads as a camel hump, and I need to check whether the bedroll and rugs sitting on top would end up buried if I increase the hump height.

I'm working through the eye size increase and highlight placement to make sure the eyes properly emerge from the head sphere's surface rather than looking sunken, while double-checking the brow ellipsoid doesn't end up overlapping awkwardly with the enlarged eye.

For the ears, I'm swapping the two spike-shaped bones for a single rounded ellipsoid instead, positioning it along the same outward direction and scaling it to look like a small elongated ear bump on the head.

Adjusting mane spike sizes and forelock placement...

I'm repositioning the three camel instances, tweaking scale factors and coordinates so the adults sit further apart and the baby camel shifts slightly, while reconsidering the yaw angle so camel 2 faces the right direction.

Computing the hip position using the forward vector gives roughly (0.16, 0.547), which lands close to one of the cushion positions near the fire — I need to check for overlap there.

I'm testing moving camel2 outward along the z-axis, but that pushes the head beyond the base radius, so it's out of bounds. I'll instead adjust camel2's yaw to roughly -1.2 radians so it faces along the edge tangent, mostly toward -x, and recompute its forward vector from there.

Checking the new position: hips land around (0.26, 0.66) with radius 0.71, head extends to about (-0.35, 0.89) with radius 0.96, both within bounds. The cushion sits at distance 0.22 from the hips, which is fine, and the rug near the fire doesn't conflict much with the hind legs, though footprints show minor overlap with a camel leg.

Now I'm checking camel1 at (-0.52, 0.5) with yaw 0.9, computing its forward vector and head position at roughly (-0.15, 0.8), then working out the hip offset.

Checking the baby's head offset puts it at roughly (-0.71,0.35), which looks fine, so I'll keep the yaw as is. I also need to verify the palm tree position near (-0.56,-0.08) with its leaning trunk doesn't overlap other elements.

Adjusting the dune function so its height is clamped to stay above the ground plane, recomputing the vertical offset so taller dunes don't poke below the sand surface. I'm also double-checking other low-lying elements like the mesa, cactus base, and pond to make sure they all sit flush with the terrain.
